posts.cooked:
I figured out last week (while away from my decks, of course; mutter mutter) that the only way to beat the Chairman is with Legacy making himself immune to a category of damage and then taking the hits for everyone. Eager to test my theory, I randomly rolled up some allies and an environment, and ended up with the Time Cataclysm.

I was doing pretty well, but toward the end of the game–I hadn’t shuffled the villain trash yet, and everyone but the Chairman had HP in the teens–the environment deck played the card Surprise Shopping Trip. If you don’t know it, its text says that whenever a card enters play, each target is dealt one melee damage.

The next card to come out of the villain deck was Prison Break. The trash had not yet been shuffled and all five underbosses were in the deck, so they all came out at once, and then each one brought out a henchman to go with.

Legacy’s Lead From the Front couldn’t protect the heroes, since the damage was being inflicted by an environment card, but that’s not the point. The point is, I wonder when exactly this damage is being inflicted. I…

Ugh, this question is complicated. Never mind, let me tell you what I did and you can tell me what I did wrong.

The first card to come out was the Deputy. I inflicted one point of damage to him, to the Operative, and to the only one of my heroes who had no armor to absorb the melee damage for a card being player. The second card to come out was the Fence, so I inflicted one point of damage to him, to the Deputy, to the Operative, and to my unarmored hero. Each card played took one less damage than the card before it, in short.

Was that how it should have happened, or did Prison Break cause each underboss to come out simultaneously, so that each one would have taken five HP of damage?

What about at the end of the turn, when each underboss brought out a henchman? Do they come into play one at a time, or separately?

Thank you for any answers, and for alleviating the headache I have inflicted upon myself.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Nothing in Sentinels happens simultaneously.  I believe you handled this correctly, with one exception.  My understanding is that one shots enter play as well, so everything currently in play (ie your unshielded hero and the Operative) should have taken damage for Prison Break.

 

Since Prison Break doesn't specify an order, you can choose what order the underbosses come into play.  This is important, because end of turn effects trigger in the order the cards came into play.  So the thugs will come into play one at a time in a fixed order determined by the order you chose for the underbosses.  If one underboss dies before they summon their thug, then that thug will not get summoned.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
It has been confirmed that when a source of an effect is destroyed, the effect ends, even if it hasn't been completed.  End of Days + Bee Bot meets those requirements.  There are no simulatenous effects in SotM, and this includes effects that damage or destroy everything.

 

Quotes from Spiff's Rules and Clarifications:

​ > destroying a card before it’s finished 

 

when a card is destroyed before it can finish its effect, any remaining effect is 
cancelled. 
 
 
for example, Ra has his “Flame Barrier” out, and a villain target deals 
all hero targets damage. The players decide to target Ra first, and Ra 
immediately retaliates, dealing enough damage to destroy the 
attacker. With the attacking target gone, there is nothing to continue 

dealing damage to the rest of the hero targets

​ > resolve each effect completely before moving on 

 

If a card has multiple effects and the first effect triggers another effect, the 
triggered effect must resolve completely before continuing with subsequent 
effects on the original card. 
 
 
example: Expatriette’s card “RPG Launcher” can remove an Ongoing or 
Environment card, and if it does, then Expatriette may deal some damage. 
If she uses “RPG Launcher” on one of Grand Warlord Voss’ “Forced 
Deployment” cards, then the effects would happen like this: 
“RPG Launcher” destroys “Forced Deployment”. “Forced Deployment” is 
immediately removed from play and placed in the Villain trash, and all of 
the minion cards are immediately put from the Villain trash into play. 
Then, Expatriette may deal her damage, including to any of the minions 
who were just put into play by “Forced Deployment”. 
 

​ > there will be times when it looks like effects in the game should happen 

simultaneously, but that is never the case. effects happen one at a time 
according to an order of events. follow the guideline below when determining 
the proper order of events: 
 
 
a) any cards with a “start of turn” or “end of turn” effect triggers those 
effects in the order the cards were played. 
 
 
for example, when the villain’s end-of-turn phase happens, all of the villain 
cards on the table that have end-of-turn effects will trigger. in this case, you 
would step through the cards in the order they were played, resolving each 
card’s end-of-turn effect and then moving on to the next in line. 
 
 
b) in any other case where two or more effects would trigger simultaneously, 
the effects may be triggered in whatever order the players choose. 
 
 
for example, if a card says to deal damage to all hero targets, the players 

may choose the order in which each instance of damage occurs.

 

Quotes hate proper formating.  Sorry about that.
